common_name: Mauna Loa Peace Lily (Large-Growing Heavy-Blooming Classic Houseplant Peace Lily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in moist, well-drained, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in deep to moderate shade; Mauna Loa grows notably larger than common peace lily selections and flowers more heavily, making it a popular choice for interior plantscaping and large indoor containers.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in deep shade, keeping the plant warm above 60°F and away from direct sun and drying drafts. Mauna Loa is a larger, more vigorous peace lily selection than the common species, bred for bigger, glossier leaves and a heavier, more reliable flush of white spathes that stand well above the foliage, making it a long-standing favorite for commercial interior plantscaping, lobbies, and large shaded containers where scale matters. Like other peace lilies it is remarkably tolerant of low indoor light, watering lapses, and general neglect, drooping dramatically when thirsty but recovering quickly once watered, and it reblooms intermittently through the year given adequate warmth and humidity. It is toxic to cats and dogs if chewed or ingested, so site it out of reach of curious pets.
sources: NASA Clean Air Study (Wolverton et al., 1989)

common_name: Elfin Creeping Fig (Miniature Tiny-Leaved Terrarium and Topiary Vine)

planting.note: Grow indoors year-round in bright, indirect light and high humidity, or move outdoors after the last frost into shade; Elfin's dwarf, dense growth and tiny quarter-inch leaves make it a favorite for terrariums, fairy gardens, and topiary forms.

directions: Grow in bright, indirect light with consistently moist, well-drained soil and high humidity, misting regularly or using a pebble tray if grown indoors where air is dry. Elfin is a dwarf sport of climbing fig selected for tiny, densely packed quarter-inch leaves and slow, compact growth that stays low and creeping rather than developing the larger juvenile leaves and vigorous climbing habit of standard creeping fig, making it especially well suited to terrariums, dish gardens, fairy gardens, and small topiary forms trained over wire frames. Its fine texture and tight growth habit also make it useful as a miniature groundcover in shaded outdoor containers in warm climates. Trim regularly to maintain shape and density, and protect it from direct sun and cold, both of which stress the fine foliage; outside zone 9's mildest microclimates it is best treated as a houseplant or brought in over winter.
